title: [FR] Show last line on stdout/stderr during command execution
body:
Currently we need to press **ctrl+r** on the bash to show all output. It would be nice to see the last line of the stdout/stderr.

For example, this is today:

```bash
! uv run pytest
  ⎿  ============================= test session starts ==============================
     platform darwin -- Python 3.11.11, pytest-8.4.1, pluggy-1.6.0
     rootdir: /Users/username/Projects/projectname
     … +7 lines (ctrl+r to expand)
```

New version could look like this

```bash
! uv run pytest
  ⎿  ============================= test session starts ==============================
     platform darwin -- Python 3.11.11, pytest-8.4.1, pluggy-1.6.0
     rootdir: /Users/username/Projects/projectname
. . .
============================== 4 passed in 0.21s ===============================
     … +6 lines (ctrl+r to expand)
```

Related to [Streaming stdout/stderr during bash command execution #1890](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/1890)
author: varun-d
